title: Understanding God
description: A tour of how Indian traditions conceive of the Divine, beginning with the Gita and the Upanishads and moving through devotional, Vedantic, Shaiva, Shakta and Sikh understandings. Each step is presented on its own terms, without ranking.

steps.title: All strung on the Divine
steps.note: Everything rests on the Divine like pearls on a thread.

steps.title: Immanent and transcendent
steps.note: All beings are in God, yet God is not confined to them.

steps.title: The Supreme Person
steps.note: Beyond the perishable and the imperishable.

steps.title: The Upanishads
steps.note: The Shvetashvatara is the most theistic of the major Upanishads; others speak of Brahman.

steps.title: Brahman
steps.note: The absolute ground of being in the Upanishads.

steps.title: Bhakti
steps.note: God known through love and devotion.

steps.title: Bhagavata Purana
steps.note: The central text of Krishna devotion.

steps.title: Vishishtadvaita
steps.note: Ramanuja: one God, with world and souls as God's body.

steps.title: Dvaita
steps.note: Madhva: God eternally distinct from souls and matter.

steps.title: Shaivism
steps.note: Shiva as the supreme Lord; Siddhanta and Kashmir views differ.

steps.title: Devi Mahatmya
steps.note: The foundational text of Goddess worship.

steps.title: Sikh philosophy
steps.note: One formless God, known through the Name and grace.

steps.title: Hukam
steps.note: The divine order in which all things move.
